newsitem.title: MEXICO: Future of Mexico soybean meal tariffs uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Future of Mexico soybean meal tariffs uncertain.

text.p: Mexico City's oil crushers were assured by the Mexican government that tariffs on U.S. soybean meal imports will not shrink this year, American Soybean Association's Mexico office said in a report.
As part of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), tariffs on U.S. soybean imports to Mexico were cut 10 percent annually from an original 15 percent.
Mexican oil crushers have been lobbying to keep the tariffs to make locally crushed meal more competitive. The tariff applies from August to January, when Mexico's harvest is strongest.

In a report obtained by Reuters, the association said a government commission on foreign trade plans to recommend the Trade Ministry (SECOFI) set aside an amount of soybeal meal to be imported duty free.

"In the meantime, the ministry of agriculture has assured its supporters that the tariff on meal will be lifted and SECOFI has assured its supporters that the tariff on meal will not be lifted. Historically the supporters of SECOFI have prevailed," the association wrote.
Weak domestic soybean crops may have forced Mexico's 1996 imports to about 3 million tonnes, up from 2.2 million tonnes in 1995.
